claim: An unrelated serializer change rides along with this generator fix. Removing the `case <= byte.MaxValue` branch changes the wire format: integer values 128..255 that used to be written as uint8 (0xcc, 2 bytes) now fall through to TryWriteUInt16 (0xcd, 3 bytes). The output is no longer the smallest encoding the MessagePack spec asks for, and it differs byte-for-byte from what the same values serialized to before. REQ-2283 asks for nothing in the serializer runtime.

claim: The reportDiagnostic wrapper drops every diagnostic whose location is not in a source tree of this compilation, including Location.None, and not only diagnostics about metadata symbols. GetPropertyIdentifierLocation returns null when the declaring syntax is not a PropertyDeclarationSyntax, such as a positional record parameter `[property: Key(...)]` in the compiling assembly. So the BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull diagnostic for such a source-declared member is now silently suppressed instead of reported. L12 only sanctions missing diagnostics for types from referenced assemblies.

claim: Unrelated wire-format change. Removing the `case <= byte.MaxValue` branch from the unsigned `MessagePackPrimitives.TryWrite` overload means values 128..255 no longer use the 2-byte uint8 form (0xcc xx). They now fall through to the 3-byte uint16 form (0xcd 00 xx). Serialized output changes size and bytes for every such value, which breaks byte-exact consumers and the MessagePack 'smallest representation' convention. REQ-2283 does not ask for this.

claim: The new GetPropertyIdentifierLocation uses `as PropertyDeclarationSyntax` and returns null for a source property whose declaring syntax is a ParameterSyntax, i.e. a positional record property. The diagnostic then gets Location.None, and the new ReportIfLocatedInCompilation wrapper drops every diagnostic that is not IsInSource. So `record R([property: Key((string)null)] int A)` declared in the compiling assembly no longer gets the BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull error, which it would get as a class property. The same wrapper also silently drops any other source-type diagnostic whose location helper returns null. That is a source symbol, not the metadata-only case covered by L12.

This changes serialized bytes for existing users, makes the output larger and non-canonical, and has nothing to do with the generator crash. Round-trip still works, but byte-exact comparisons, hashes, and fixtures break.

claim: The wrapper that filters diagnostics by compilation drops every diagnostic whose location is not in a syntax tree of the current compilation. claim: Dropping the `case <= byte.MaxValue` branch in the unsigned-integer writer means values 128..255 now fall through to TryWriteUInt16 and are encoded as uint16 (0xcd + 2 bytes) instead of uint8 (0xcc + 1 byte). This changes the wire format and is not canonical or compact. Output grows, and byte-for-byte compatibility with prior versions and with other implementations is lost. Deserialization still works, but any code that compares serialized bytes or hashes them (signatures, caches, tests with exact byte expectations) breaks. The change is unrelated to the generator/analyzer crash in REQ-2283. There is no direct deserialization-safety hole, but it is an unrelated runtime behavior change that affects canonical encoding, which matters if the bytes are signed or hashed.
